theorem_title: Exact membership in terminal completion enumeration
theorem_formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ReportingHostTerminalChoices.mem_choices {h J : ℕ} (q : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.GlobalEncoding.GlobalOutput h J) (k : ℕ)
    (S : Finset (_root_.ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J (464*h))) :
    S ∈ _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ReportingHostTerminalChoices.choices q k ↔ S ⊆ _root_.ThreeSum.BlockForced.remaining (_root_.ThreeSum.BlockRows.prefixIndices J k) (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockForced.outputRows q) ∧ S.card=(J-k)*h := by sorry
theorem_natural_language_statement:
Let $h,J,k\in\mathbb N$, $q$ a global output record, and $S$ a finite subset of the $J\cdot464h$ block coordinates. Let $R_k(q)$ be the remaining query-coordinate set after the first $k$ blocks. Then

$$S\in\operatorname{choices}(q,k)\iff S\subseteq R_k(q)\ \wedge\ |S|=(J-k)h.$$

This characterizes every enumerated terminal completion exactly, including natural-subtraction boundary cases.
